module_title: Important Days - National Birth Anniversaries and Global Awareness Milestones
introduction: This intermediate tier transitions into core Indian 'National Days' which are celebrated to commemorate the birthdays or major breakthroughs of iconic Indian statesmen, scientists, and sports legends. It also loops in heavy humanitarian global dates.

core_concepts.title: National Youth Day (January 12)
core_concepts.description: Celebrated to honor the birth anniversary of Swami Vivekananda, one of India's greatest spiritual philosophers, whose teachings heavily targeted youth empowerment.

core_concepts.title: National Science Day (February 28)
core_concepts.description: Commemorates the landmark discovery of the 'Raman Effect' by prominent Indian physicist Sir C.V. Raman on February 28, 1928, which fetched him the Nobel Prize.

core_concepts.title: National Sports Day (August 29)
core_concepts.description: Marks the birth anniversary of Major Dhyan Chand, India's legendary hockey wizard. The President of India distributes the National Sports Awards (like the Khel Ratna and Arjuna Awards) on this day.

core_concepts.title: Good Governance Day (December 25)
core_concepts.description: Established in 2014 to honor former Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee on his birth anniversary, aiming to foster accountability in government administration.

core_concepts.title: Human Rights Day (December 10)
core_concepts.description: Celebrated globally to honor the United Nations General Assembly's adoption and proclamation of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights (UDHR) on December 10, 1948.

important_entities.name: January 12
important_entities.significance: Aims to propagate Vivekananda's principles of character building among the youth.

important_entities.name: February 28
important_entities.significance: Celebrates scientific innovation; links directly to Sir C.V. Raman's breakthrough.

important_entities.name: August 29
important_entities.significance: Commemorates the legacy of Major Dhyan Chand.

important_entities.name: December 10
important_entities.significance: The official day when the annual Nobel Prizes are formally presented to recipients in Stockholm and Oslo.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation:
This is the most highly favored trap used by TCS examiners! Note the shifts:
- **National Youth Day** = January 12 | **International Youth Day** = August 12.
- **National Teachers' Day** = September 5 (Dr. Radhakrishnan) | **World Teachers' Day** = October 5 (Exactly one month later).
Statement-based questions often claim that February 28 is Sir C.V. Raman's birthday. This is a trap! It is the anniversary of the *discovery* of the Raman Effect. His actual birthday is November 7.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: India's Teachers' Day is Sept 5, World is Oct 5. National Youth Day is Jan 12, International Youth Day is Aug 12 (Same date numerical digits, completely different months).

exam_strategy_tips: Modern exams don't just ask for the date; they test your knowledge of the *underlying reason* or personality. Always map the day to its respective historical context.
